mainTopic: אבק לשון הרע; קפידא versus מראה מקום in the dispute about local custom for documents; and whether a written witness and a spoken witness combine.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב's teaching about לשון הרע. He says most people fail in גזל, some in עריות, and everyone in לשון הרע, and the גמרא explains that 'everyone' means only אבק לשון הרע, a faint trace of it. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about פשוט and מקושר documents, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says everything follows local custom. רב אשי explains that both sides accept local custom. They argue only in a town that uses both kinds of documents, when the person asked for a פשוט and got a מקושר: was he being strict (קפידא), or just pointing out an option (מראה מקום)? אביי adds that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר all hold מראה מקום, and the גמרא proves this from משניות in קידושין and גיטין. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that a פשוט with one witness is invalid. אביי answers that even one written witness plus one spoken witness do not combine. אמימר disagrees with אביי, and רב אשי points out that the question on the משנה then comes back; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב meant only a trace of לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question. רב's statement about לשון הרע means only אבק לשון הרע, a faint trace of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant a 'dust' (a trace) of לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question from just before this section. It explains that רב was talking about a light trace of לשון הרע, not real לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to say that every person speaks actual לשון הרע. So the גמרא narrows רב's words to אבק לשון הרע, which is much harder to avoid. This makes רב's claim believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals a corrected reading
'Dust' of evil speech; a hint or trace of לשון הרע
Evil or harmful speech about others

phrases.english: Rather, [he meant] the dust of evil speech.
phrases.notes: This answers a question at the end of the previous page about רב's list of sins that nobody escapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question that the גמרא raised just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to say that everyone speaks real לשון הרע
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means only a trace of לשון הרע

steps.title: Most people fail in robbery, some in עריות, all in לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: most people stumble in גזל, a minority in עריות, and everyone in לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Most people sin in robbery, a minority in forbidden relations, and everyone in evil speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב about which sins people commonly fall into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ranks three sins by how common they are. גזל is common because people are not careful with money. עריות is less common. לשון הרע seems to reach everyone, and that claim is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority
Minority
Robbery; taking what belongs to someone else
Forbidden relationships

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The majority [sin] in robbery,
and a minority in forbidden relations,
and everyone in evil speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching of רב on the same theme of לשון הרע
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most people fail in גזל, a minority in עריות, and everyone in לשון הרע

steps.title: Can everyone really speak לשון הרע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised. Does רב really mean that every single person speaks לשון הרע?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it enter your mind that everyone sins in evil speech?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last part of רב's statement because it sounds too extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'everyone' speaks real לשון הרע would mean that no one at all is free of a serious sin. That does not seem possible, so the גמרא pushes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? A way of saying something is hard to accept

phrases.english: In evil speech, can it enter your mind?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone speaks לשון הרע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is not reasonable that every person commits real לשון הרע

steps.title: Again: רב meant only a trace of לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. רב means אבק לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant a trace of evil speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by narrowing רב's words to a faint trace of לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real לשון הרע is not universal, but small hints and indirect remarks are something almost nobody avoids completely. So 'everyone' is true about אבק לשון הרע.
steps.whatToRemember: When רב says 'everyone' fails in לשון הרע, the גמרא explains he means אבק לשון הרע, the faint traces of it that almost no one avoids.

phrases.english: Rather, [he meant] the dust of evil speech.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the statement
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone speaks only אבק לשון הרע

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: everything follows local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about documents and quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says everything follows the custom of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Everything follows the custom of the region.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about פשוט (plain) and מקושר (tied) documents. It quotes the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל to set up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in the משנה disqualified a document written in the wrong form, plain instead of tied or tied instead of plain. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that it all depends on what is done locally.

keyTerms.meaning: The custom of the region

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Everything is according to the custom of the region.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר הַכֹּל כְּמִנְהַג הַמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of לשון הרע and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The form of a document follows local custom

steps.title: Does the תנא קמא reject local custom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the תנא קמא really disagrees that local custom matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does the תנא קמא not hold of regional custom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled that there seems to be an argument at all. Following local custom seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is disagreeing, it would mean the תנא קמא ignores local custom. That would be very strange, so the גמרא needs to explain what the actual difference between them is.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
He does not hold of it

phrases.english: And the first Tanna,
does he not hold of regional custom?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לֵית לֵיהּ מִנְהַג מְדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the dispute quoted in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the תנא קמא disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one would reject something as basic as local custom

steps.title: רב אשי: a clear request shows the person was particular
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי begins his answer with a case where both sides agree. In a place with only one custom, the person asked for that kind of document and the scribe made the other kind. Everyone agrees the person was particular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In a place where the custom is plain documents, and he told him 'Make me a plain one,' and he went and made a tied one, he was particular. Where the custom is tied, and he told him 'Make me a tied one,' and he went and made a plain one, he was particular.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts answering the question by giving cases where everyone agrees. In a place with a single custom, the person asked for that form and the scribe did the opposite. The next step gives the case where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the town uses only one form, and the person asks for exactly that form, both the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agree he was particular (קפידא). A document made the other way was not made the way he wanted. So the תנא קמא does not reject local custom; their argument must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where it is customary
A plain, ordinary document
A tied (folded and stitched) document
Being particular; it shows he truly cared

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רב אשי as saying the תנא קמא ignores custom. In his cases the person asked for exactly what the custom already is, and saying it out loud is what shows he was particular.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept local custom. Where only one form is customary and the person asked for it, everyone agrees he was particular if the scribe made the other form.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
In a place where they are accustomed to plain [documents],
and he said to him, 'Make me a plain one,'
phrases.notes: The person is speaking to the scribe here.

phrases.english: and he went and made him a tied one —
he was particular.
[Where] they are accustomed to tied [documents],
and he said to him, 'Make me a tied one,'
and he went and made him a plain one —
he was particular.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי בְּאַתְרָא דִּנְהִיגִי פָּשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by defining the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא ignores local custom
steps.terutzMaskana: In a place with only one custom, everyone agrees the request shows the person was particular. The dispute is limited to a different case, given in step 8.

steps.title: The real case of the disagreement: a place that uses both kinds of documents
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי continues: the dispute is in a place that uses both פשוט and מקושר. The person asked for a פשוט and got a מקושר. The תנא קמא says he was strict. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he was only pointing out an easy option.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree in a place where people use both ordinary and tied documents. Someone told the scribe, 'Make me an ordinary one,' and the scribe made a tied one. One Sage says the person really cared which kind he got. The other Sage says he was just showing the scribe an easier option.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אשי's answer by showing the exact case where the two opinions in the משנה really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, the person asked for the one kind of document that is already the local custom, so his request clearly showed he cared. Here both kinds are normal in the town, so his request could mean two things. The תנא קמא reads it as a strict demand (קפידא), so the document is not valid. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads it as 'you may make the easy one if you like' (מראה מקום), so the tied one is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary document, written flat and signed at the bottom
A tied document: folded and sewn, with witnesses signing on the folds. It is more work to make.
Being strict. The person really insists on exactly what he asked for.
Literally 'he is showing him a place.' He is only pointing out an option, not making a demand.
One Sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ignores what the person said. He agrees the person asked for a פשוט. He just understands the request as 'you don't have to bother with the harder kind,' not as 'I refuse anything else.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of מראה מקום, and the rest of the sugya builds on it. אביי will use it to tie together several תנאים.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is
in a place where people use both ordinary and tied documents,
and he said to him (the scribe): "Make me an ordinary one,"
and the scribe went and made him a tied one;
one Sage holds: he was being strict,
phrases.notes: This 'one Sage' is the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: he was just showing him an option.
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He means: 'You can save yourself the work of a tied one if you want.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב אשי's answer. Step 7 gave the case where everyone agrees; this gives the case where they argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the תנא קמא ignores local custom altogether.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides follow local custom. They only argue when both kinds are common and the request is unclear: is it strict, or just pointing out an option?

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים all hold 'מראה מקום'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר all share the view that a person's instruction is often just pointing out an option.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר all hold that 'he is just showing him an option.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a new statement that groups three תנאים together under the idea of מראה מקום. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא shows where each one says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that started in our משנה about documents now becomes a wider principle. When someone gives instructions, these three תנאים do not assume he insists on every detail. אביי is claiming they share one approach, and he will need to prove it for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them hold

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns one opinion in our משנה into a principle that shows up in other places in ש״ס, like קידושין.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Elazar:
all of them hold:
he is just showing him an option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מראה מקום idea from step 8 and applies it to two more תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר all hold that an instruction is often just pointing out an option, not a strict demand.

steps.title: The source for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is what we just learned
steps.stepSummary: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the proof is the case we just explained about the documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: this is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving אביי's list one name at a time. The first one is easy: it is the case we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on the פשוט/מקושר document, as explained in step 8, already shows the idea of מראה מקום. So no new source is needed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we already said

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: this is what we just said.
phrases.notes: He means the document case from step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first proof for אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds מראה מקום
steps.raayaSupportSource: His opinion in our משנה, as explained in step 8

steps.title: The source for רבי שמעון: misleading her for the better
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, the גמרא quotes a משנה in קידושין. There he says that if she was misled in a way that is better for her, the קידושין still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון: as we learned in a משנה, רבי שמעון says: if he misled her to her advantage, she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof for the second name on אביי's list, רבי שמעון, from a משנה about קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the woman agreed to be betrothed on certain terms, but she actually got something better. רבי שמעון says the קידושין works. This shows he does not treat her words as a strict demand. She was only saying the least she would accept, which is exactly the idea of מראה מקום.

keyTerms.meaning: He misled her to her advantage. She got something better than she was told.
She is betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'misled' means the קידושין is fake or tricky here. The change was only in her favor, so רבי שמעון holds her words were never a strict condition.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon: as we learned in a mishna,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קידושין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
if he misled her to her advantage,
she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second proof for אביי's list, after רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds מראה מקום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in קידושין: 'אם הטעה לשבח הרי זו מקודשת'

steps.title: Proof that רבי אלעזר also sees instructions as just pointing out an option
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in גיטין. A woman tells her agent to receive her גט in one place, and he receives it somewhere else. The תנא קמא says the גט is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר holds this too, as a משנה teaches: a woman told her agent, 'Receive my גט for me in place X,' and he received it in place Y. The גט is invalid, but רבי אלעזר says it is valid. One side holds she was particular. The other side holds she was just telling him where to find her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last proof for אביי's statement. It shows that רבי אלעזר also treats a person's instruction as just pointing out an option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads the woman's words as a firm condition, so changing the place ruins the agency. רבי אלעזר reads her words as helpful advice about where the husband would be, so the agent did not really go against her wishes. This is the same split as the document case and the קידושין case.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive my גט for me. She is appointing an agent to accept the divorce on her behalf.
Rules it valid
Being particular. The instruction is a firm requirement.
Pointing out a place. The instruction is only a helpful suggestion.

steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs show one idea. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר each say that a person's specific instruction is often just pointing out an option, not a strict demand.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar — as we learned in a Mishnah:
The woman who said:
"Receive my bill of divorce for me in such-and-such a place,"
and he received it for her in another place — it is invalid;
and Rabbi Elazar rules it valid.
One Sage holds: she was particular,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מַרְאֶה מָקוֹם הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: she was just pointing out a place to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's three-part list of proofs that began in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי אלעזר holds an instruction is just pointing out an option
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין about an agent who received the גט in a different place than the woman named

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say a single-witness document is invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It agrees that the rule about a מקושר with only two witnesses needed to be taught. But it asks why the משנה tells us that a פשוט with only one witness is invalid, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a פשוט with one witness written in it is invalid. It makes sense that the משנה had to say a מקושר with two witnesses is invalid. You might have thought that since two witnesses are normally enough, they are enough here too. So the משנה teaches that it is invalid. But a פשוט with just one witness? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and challenges one of its rules as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are usually enough, so a beginner might think a מקושר with two signatures is fine. That makes it a real lesson. But one witness is never enough for a document, so saying a פשוט with one witness is invalid seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense regarding... (it sets up a contrast with a part that does not make sense)
You might have thought...
It teaches us
It's obvious! (why say it?)

phrases.english: [An ordinary document in which one witness is written, etc.]
It makes sense regarding a tied document

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עֵדִים, פָּסוּל – אִיצְטְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: with two witnesses written in it, that it is invalid — that needed to be said,
since it would have entered your mind to say:
since in general it is valid —
here too it is valid;
so it teaches us that it is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פָּשׁוּט שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ עֵד אֶחָד –
phrases.english: But an ordinary document with one witness written in it —
that's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מְקוּשָּׁר שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא leaves the discussion of instructions and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a פשוט with one witness is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One witness is never enough for a document, so the rule seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: אביי: even one written witness plus one spoken witness is invalid
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה is teaching a new point. Even if one witness signed the פשוט and a second witness comes and testifies out loud, the document is still invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the rule was needed to teach that the document is invalid even with one witness in writing and one witness speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by showing what new point the משנה is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought that a written witness and a spoken witness add up to two witnesses. אביי says the משנה teaches that they do not combine. The document still counts as a single-witness document.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (introduces the new case the rule is really teaching)
In writing (signed on the document)
By mouth (testifying out loud)

phrases.english: Abaye said: it was needed only
to teach that even with one witness in writing
and one witness by mouth, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: The words "it is invalid" are not in the text, but the גמרא assumes them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' question from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the rule a new case that is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A written witness and a spoken witness might combine to make two valid witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not combine. The document is still invalid.

steps.title: אמימר rules such a document is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אמימר actually ruled that a document with one witness in writing and one witness testifying out loud is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר ruled that a document with one witness in writing and one witness speaking is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that אמימר ruled the opposite of what אביי just said. This sets up רב אשי's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the two kinds of witnesses do not combine. אמימר treated them as joining together to make two witnesses. This sets up a clash between the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruled it valid
Orally (out loud)

phrases.english: Ameimar ruled valid a case of one witness in writing
and one witness orally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a ruling that goes against אביי's explanation in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One written witness plus one spoken witness make a valid document.

steps.title: רב אשי asks אמימר about אביי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר: what about אביי, who said such a document is invalid?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: and what about אביי's ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises אביי's opinion against אמימר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Although it is worded as a question, it works as a challenge. אביי explicitly said this case is invalid, so how could אמימר rule it valid?

keyTerms.meaning: And what about אביי's statement?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
And what about that ruling of Abaye?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling from step 15 using אביי's view from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that the document is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי said this exact case is invalid.

steps.title: אמימר: I don't hold like אביי
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers, 'I did not hear it.' The גמרא explains that this means he does not agree with אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: I did not hear it. That is, I don't hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי by saying he disagrees with אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I did not hear it' does not mean he never learned אביי's statement. It is a polite way of saying he rejects it. So אמימר keeps his ruling that the two witnesses combine.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it
I do not hold like it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't take 'I did not hear it' literally. The גמרא itself explains that it means 'I disagree.'
steps.whatToRemember: There is a dispute. אביי says one written witness plus one spoken witness do not make a valid document. אמימר says they do.

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not hear it —
meaning to say, I do not hold like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי – כְּלוֹמַר, לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Openly disagrees with the opposing authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אמימר must either accept אביי or explain why אביי's ruling does not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר simply disagrees with אביי and keeps his own ruling.

steps.title: Without אביי's explanation, the question on the משנה returns
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells אמימר that if he rejects אביי's view, the original difficulty with the משנה is back: why would the משנה need to say that a פשוט with one witness is invalid?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the difficulty returns!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר. If אמימר does not accept אביי's explanation, the old question about the משנה (from step 13) is unanswered again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's ruling was the answer to the question 'Why does the משנה teach something so obvious?' Once אמימר rejects that ruling, the answer is gone. The question of why the משנה says a פשוט with one witness is invalid comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But, if so: here it means 'if you reject that answer'
A difficulty, a question that has not been answered

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question from step 13, coming back because אמימר rejected the answer that אביי gave.

phrases.english: But [then] there is a difficulty
phrases.notes: רב אשי means the question from step 13: why does the משנה bother saying a פשוט with one witness is invalid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from אמימר's statement in step 17 that he does not agree with אביי. It shows that this position brings back the problem from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's position that a document with one witness in writing and one witness testifying out loud is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's ruling explained why the משנה needed to say that a פשוט with one witness is invalid. Without that ruling, the משנה's statement seems obvious again, and nothing explains why it was taught.
